title: Two years of crypto headlines scored at ingestion, not retroactively — open 3-month slice with hourly prices
author: l3xxxy

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: scored once and never revised is what almost every sentiment set gets wrong. with the ~10 minute lag, does a headline from 14:58 get joined to the 15:00 bar or the 16:00 one?

replies.author: l3xxxy
replies.body: The bar that opened at 14:00, i.e. the bar that contains published\_at. That matches how you'd run it live: at the close of the 14:00 bar, which is the open of the 15:00 one, you take all headlines published during that hour, and by then they're already scored. So the news of a bar is joined to that bar, and the first price you act on is the next bar's open. ingested\_at is there if you want to check the timing yourself.

replies.author: l3xxxy
replies.body: One correction on the lag itself: the \~10 minutes is an average, not a fixed delay added to every headline. Scoring runs every 15 minutes, so a headline published at 14:58 is picked up by the next run, a couple of minutes later. The headlines that wait longest are the ones published right after a run, and they're still scored well inside the same bar. So the late-bar headlines are the ones with the least lag, not the most, and the 15:00 open is available for them.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: that join is fine if the fill is at that bar's close. the leak is the lag: a headline published at 14:58 doesn't get its score until about 15:08, so it isn't actually known at the 15:00 close it's joined to. joining on scored_at instead of published_at fixes it.
